title: Help a noob understand
author: Arolasgaming
selftext:
For as long as I can remember I have had game ideaS floating around in my head. I would love to be able to build these using ai. From what I have seen it is 100% doable. 

I have been trying to watch videos of people explaining but it doesn't make a whole lot of sense, to be honest. 

I know Claude is the go to. Currently I am trying to use Codex as I have a current got subscription.

I have also experimented with a few engines over the last few days (Godot, Unity and URE) 

I think the biggest thing I um not understanding is how all the different tools you need linked together in order to be able to "vibe code" a game. 

My experience with vibe coding is with Base44 to build apps, which is super straight forward to build apps. 

I also understand to build system upon system and not try to do the whole thing at once. 

If anyone can send me a DM and either give me a good explanation of how this all works and how to get started. Or point me to a resource you used to get started. 

OR if there happens to be anyone  making games in Melbourne Australia willing to show me how it works side by side that would be sick. 

I have ideas but not the know-how.

comments.author: Disastrous-Round-150
comments.body:
Do as I do! 100% from scratch and 100% procedural, zero game engines and zero game assets. It sounds like more work but it's quite the opposite. I can turn a well thought through game idea into a working game prototype within 1 hour with GPT 6 Astra set at max in work mode.

This way I can focus on game mechanics and game play what really matters in a game, without having to think of making game assets and game engines. Assets and engines waste a lot of toll usage time with back and forth with the AI.

It's better to have a full working game prototype with the game mechanics and game play dialed in before going to the step of making game assets and choosing a game engine which you see fit for your game. Or you can simply stay 100% procedural the procedural capabilities of current AIs are astonishing and without a game engine you are 100% in charge of what is happening underneath.

comments.author: MinimumError1828
comments.body:
My setup:

Claude in Visual studio code.

Claude hooked up to Blender

Claude hooked up to sound effect generator

Claude hooked up to Godot

Install the mantle skill atlas to grab any skill you need 

Use google spreadsheet, hook it up to claude, use that as your database for all data you need to keep track of, like enemy hit points and damage and such.

Go tell it your idea and watch it code something in godot, then use blender and the other stuff to create whatever it's missing.

comments.author: SidAkrita
comments.body:
Hey from the other side of the planet. First thing first, AI is totally able to create games for you, but maybe not as fast and easily as you might think, and depending on the scope of your project it might even be impossible right now.

Nonetheless, first rule if you are new to game dev : ask your ai. A lot of content creators are here to get views, a lot of content is just slop or pure garbage trying to sell you some sort of thing to help you build the next best SaaS.

Some people use a lot of tools, some just one, some use AI just for some parts... I'd say for you, stick to Unity or Godot, don't go near Unreal for now, it's really complex. You can even use a JS framework, or MonoGame, pygame or Love2D. You don't have to code or understand how it works, just talk to your AI and see where it sends you.

The other tools you might need are when you'll have to tweak game design things, create a special pipeline for your assets, a control board for a multiplayer game. I suppose you're not here right now, just use your Codex subscription and use this to start up a Godot project, it can download the last release, create the project, make a prototype and build it for you to try it.

If you don't want to go too deep in technical parts, do this, then play the game, take screenshots of what you like and dislike, and send it to a new session explaining what you want to change. You'll learn a lot like this, at some point you'll want to use git, some sort of issue system, PRs, and so on but stick to the basics for now.

  
And remember to ask your AI ! And use new sessions regularly, do not throw everything into one single session.

That is it really.

if you need a step-by-step guide, just source like 5-10 tutorials and ask Claude to summarize the tutorials as steps for you...

comments.author: NebulaRisingGame
comments.body:
I would recommend reading up on (use claude) to give you high level playbook/documentation on best practices for architecture and setup for the type of game you want to build.

Since you are fully new, start with something stupid simple and keep the scope small.  Then iterate on it, make sure to use code managment (git repo), once it looks good iterate some more and make claude explain what its doing in its responses like you're a 10yr old.  To start building a foundation of knowledge of building software in general.  You are starting at zero.  Baby steps or you will get way in over your head very very quickly and you won't be able to get out.
